variations.name: Solid-media heat batteries delivering steam and hot air
variations.description: Electric resistance elements heat cheap solid media (firebrick, carbon blocks, slag granulate, sand, rock, alloy blocks) to 400-1,800C when renewable power is cheap, then discharge continuous steam or hot air (or power via thermophotovoltaics), letting factories run on intermittent electricity without boilers.

companies.name: Rondo Energy
companies.what: Refractory-brick heat battery (RHB) charged resistively, discharging high-pressure steam and hot air for fuels, food, chemicals and cement plants.
companies.signal: World's largest 100 MWh heat battery in daily commercial operation in California (Oct 2025); EUR 75M project funding from Breakthrough Energy Catalyst + EIB; 100 MWh Heineken/EDP brewery deal in Portugal.

companies.name: Antora Energy
companies.what: Solid carbon-block thermal batteries that emit heat as radiant light, plus thermophotovoltaic heat-to-power modules.
companies.signal: $150M Series B (Decarbonization Partners), >$230M total; ARPA-E $14.5M SCALEUP; 5 GWh system commissioning at POET ethanol plant, South Dakota; novel Otter Tail Power tariff.

companies.name: Kraftblock
companies.what: Granulate storage made from recycled steel-slag handling up to ~1,300C, packaged into power-to-heat systems.
companies.signal: EUR 20M Series B (Shell Ventures, 2023); 9 MW / 70 MWh system electrifying PepsiCo's Netherlands fryer lines with Eneco; Tata Steel pilot.

companies.name: MGA Thermal
companies.what: Miscibility-gap-alloy blocks (graphite + aluminum) storing latent heat and discharging steam directly via integrated steam generation.
companies.signal: AU$17M raised 2025 (>AU$50M total) entering commercial scale-up; 5 MWh steam-integrated demonstrator commissioned April 2025; ARENA-funded FEED studies and 180 MWh prefeasibility.

companies.name: Brenmiller Energy
companies.what: Crushed-rock bGen modules charged electrically or by waste heat, discharging steam for factories and hospitals.
companies.signal: NASDAQ-listed (BNRG); ~32 MWh bGen operating at Tempo/Heineken beverage plant in Israel; additional units in Europe and US pipeline.

companies.name: Electrified Thermal Solutions
companies.what: Electrically conductive firebrick (Joule Hive) that is both heating element and storage, delivering air up to ~1,800C for cement, glass and steel.
companies.signal: $19M Series A (Jan 2025) plus >$40M in DOE awards; first commercial-scale Joule Hive thermal battery energized (announced Feb 2026).

companies.name: Polar Night Energy
companies.what: Sand batteries storing electricity as ~500C heat in low-grade sand/crushed soapstone for district and industrial heat.
companies.signal: 1 MW / 100 MWh commercial sand battery operating in Pornainen, Finland; 2 MW / 250 MWh unit for Lahti Energia's Vaaksy network under construction.

companies.name: Magaldi Green Energy
companies.what: Fluidized sand-bed thermal storage (MGTES) from a century-old Italian bulk-materials-handling group, discharging steam for industry.
companies.signal: MW-scale MGTES demonstrator operating in Italy; partnerships to supply industrial green steam leveraging parent group's manufacturing base.

variations.name: Molten-salt, molten-hydroxide, and phase-change industrial heat storage
variations.description: Stores off-peak electricity in molten salts, hydroxides, concrete or phase-change materials at 250-700C and discharges on demand as process steam - more engineering complexity than bricks but compact, pumpable, and able to deliver steady isothermal output.

companies.name: Kyoto Group
companies.what: Heatcube modular molten-salt battery delivering industrial steam, sold partly as heat-as-a-service.
companies.signal: Euronext Growth Oslo-listed; Heatcube #2 inaugurated at KALL Ingredients (Hungary) Oct 2025; EUR 4M Nefco loan for international scale-up.

companies.name: Hyme Energy
companies.what: Molten hydroxide salt storage above 500C (Seaborg spinout) with patented corrosion control, targeting 24/7 industrial steam.
companies.signal: $26M raised; global agreement with Arla incl. planned 200 MWh system at Holstebro dairy (target 2029); commercialization partnership with Sulzer (Mar 2025).

companies.name: EnergyNest
companies.what: Modular concrete (Heatcrete) thermal batteries for steam and heat at industrial sites, offered as financed turnkey systems.
companies.signal: EUR 110M Infracapital investment; 10 MW / 40 MWh power-to-heat system at tesa Hamburg; Avery Dennison Belgium operating since 2023; new CEO Feb 2025.

companies.name: 1414 Degrees
companies.what: Molten-silicon phase-change storage (SiBox) discharging very high-temperature clean heat.
companies.signal: ASX-listed; SiBox demonstration module testing; progress slow and funding-constrained relative to brick rivals.

companies.name: Azelio
companies.what: Aluminum-alloy PCM storage at 600C discharged through Stirling engines (TES.POD) for distributed heat and power.
companies.signal: Filed for bankruptcy July 2023 after failing to secure financing; Stirling and TES assets bought by TEXEL Energy.

variations.white_space: Salts and PCMs carry corrosion, freeze-protection and balance-of-plant costs that dirt-cheap brick/rock/sand systems avoid - Azelio's 2023 bankruptcy and 1414 Degrees' slow grind show the squeeze; the defensible niche is compact isothermal discharge and direct >500C steam where solid media and steam quality struggle (Hyme's hydroxide bet), plus retrofit of existing CSP salt supply chains.

variations.name: Industrial and steam-generating heat pumps, MVR, and chemical heat transformers
variations.description: Compresses ambient or waste heat - via mechanical heat pumps, vapor recompression, or absorption chemistry - to deliver 100-200C hot water and steam at 2-6x boiler efficiency, the workhorse route for electrifying low- and mid-temperature process heat in food, beverage, paper and chemicals.

companies.name: AtmosZero
companies.what: Standardized air-source 'Boiler 2.0' modular heat pump producing 150 psig steam as a drop-in boiler replacement.
companies.signal: $28.5M raised; first unit delivering steam at New Belgium Brewing (Fort Collins) in 2025; awarded up to $24.3M in 48C federal tax credits; Loveland, CO factory.

companies.name: Skyven Technologies
companies.what: Arcturus steam-generating heat pump upgrading factory waste heat to steam, installed at no capex under a steam-as-a-service model.
companies.signal: First pilot measured COP ~6.5 (2025) with target of 8; DOE-backed; shared-savings deployments alongside existing gas boilers.

companies.name: Karman Industries
companies.what: Rocket-turbomachinery-derived high-speed centrifugal heat pumps for industrial steam (team ~1/3 ex-SpaceX/Rocket Lab).
companies.signal: $31.5M raised across three rounds (Riot, Space VC, 8090 Industries); emerged from stealth Sept 2024.

companies.name: Heaten
companies.what: Norwegian piston-compressor HeatBooster HTHP delivering up to ~165C+ sink temperatures from industrial waste heat.
companies.signal: Commercial pilots in Europe and US; cited among the leading steam-producing heat pump makers entering factories in 2025-26.

companies.name: Olvondo Technology
companies.what: HighLift 750 kW helium reverse-Stirling heat pump making 200C steam from low-grade waste heat (pharma references incl. AstraZeneca).
companies.signal: Global distribution partnership with Tetra Pak (2025) for food & beverage; multiple operating European installations.

companies.name: Futraheat
companies.what: TurboClaw oil-free low-speed turbo-compressor heat pump recovering 70C waste heat to deliver up to 150C/steam.
companies.signal: UK field pilots; 500 kW-1 MW units unveiled 2024; grant-backed early commercial stage.

companies.name: Qpinch
companies.what: Chemical heat transformer (phosphoric-acid cycle mimicking ATP/ADP) upgrading industrial waste heat ~100C without large compressors.
companies.signal: Industrial units at major chemical/port sites in Antwerp cluster; claims ~50% heat-consumption savings; IEA heat-pump conference featured.

companies.name: GEA
companies.what: Global process-equipment incumbent supplying large ammonia/CO2 industrial heat pumps and MVR evaporators, dominant in dairy and food.
companies.signal: Hundreds of industrial heat-pump and MVR references worldwide; named among proven steam-HP suppliers scaling US/EU installs.

companies.name: MAN Energy Solutions
companies.what: Multi-MW industrial and district heat pumps and ETES (e.g., ~50 MW seawater CO2 heat pump at Esbjerg, Denmark).
companies.signal: Operating utility-scale heat pump references; order book across European district and industrial heat.

companies.name: Piller Blowers & Compressors
companies.what: High-performance MVR blowers/compressors for steam recompression in evaporation and drying processes.
companies.signal: Long-established German manufacturer; named among key suppliers proving steam-producing heat pump technology.

variations.name: Electric resistance and electrode boilers for process steam
variations.description: Resistance and high-voltage electrode boilers convert electricity directly to steam or hot water at up to ~75 MW per unit with near-instant ramping - mature, low-capex hardware that pairs naturally with volatile power prices and hybrid gas-electric operation.

companies.name: PARAT Halvorsen
companies.what: Norwegian leader in high-voltage electrode boilers (IEH) up to 75 MW / 85 barg steam with 30-second standby-to-full-load for grid-interactive operation.
companies.signal: 3x50 MW hot-water electrode boilers delivered to Vattenfall (NL); 10 MW steam unit at Fujifilm Europe; North Sea platform electrification orders.

companies.name: Vapor Power International
companies.what: US manufacturer of electrode and electric resistance steam boilers and generators for industrial process steam.
companies.signal: Decades-installed base across North American industry; part of Thermon Group since 2021 acquisition.

companies.name: Cleaver-Brooks
companies.what: Major US boiler maker offering electric and electrode boiler lines alongside conventional packaged boilers for hybrid fleets.
companies.signal: Broad installed base and dealer network; electric line expanding as US sites hedge gas exposure.

companies.name: Chromalox
companies.what: Electric process heating specialist (Spirax Group) supplying medium-voltage electrode steam boilers and immersion process heaters.
companies.signal: Part of Spirax Group since 2017; supplies DirectConnect medium-voltage electrification systems globally.

companies.name: Precision Boilers
companies.what: US manufacturer of electric steam boilers and storage water heaters for industrial and institutional steam loads.
companies.signal: Long-running US installed base; benefitting from electrification retrofits.

variations.white_space: The hardware is commoditized century-old technology held by a handful of boiler makers, so differentiation has moved to economics: the open ground is grid-interactive 'boiler-as-battery' dispatch software, demand-charge management, and heat-as-a-service wrappers that make electric steam pencil against cheap gas - not new steel.

variations.name: Advanced electric heating: induction, infrared, microwave, plasma, e-beam, and rotodynamic heaters
variations.description: Puts electric heat precisely where it is needed at up to 1,700C+ via electromagnetic induction, infrared emitters, microwaves, plasma torches, electron beams, or turbomachinery that converts shaft power to heat through shock waves - replacing burners inside existing furnaces, kilns and reactors.

companies.name: Coolbrook
companies.what: RotoDynamic Heater/Reactor using supersonic turbomachinery to heat process gas to ~1,700C for cement, steel and chemicals.
companies.signal: World's first commercial RotoDynamic Heater deal with Adani Cement (Nov 2025, ~60,000 tCO2/yr); pilot operating at Brightlands (NL); Nefco financing; partners incl. ABB, CRH, UltraTech.

companies.name: PyroGenesis
companies.what: TSX-listed plasma-torch maker replacing natural-gas burners in aluminum remelting furnaces and iron-ore pelletizing.
companies.signal: Constellium industrial contract (Aug 2025) with torch system delivered Mar 2026; 2025 furnace-electrification trials with Rio Tinto; 4.5 MW torch delivered to US defense client.

companies.name: Tetronics Technologies
companies.what: Veteran UK DC plasma-arc furnace supplier for metals recovery, hazardous waste and decarbonized high-temperature processing.
companies.signal: 86 plasma installations globally; customer PGM-recovery plasma plant reached full operation Dec 2024; UK NDA nuclear-waste-treatment award Jan 2025.

companies.name: Pyrowave
companies.what: Industrial microwave platform for electrified chemistry, notably microwave depolymerization of polystyrene with Michelin.
companies.signal: Michelin partnership and commercial demonstration units in Canada/Europe; positioning microwave as precise electrification of chemical process heat.

companies.name: Inductotherm Group
companies.what: World's largest supplier of induction melting and heating systems for metals industries.
companies.signal: Thousands of induction furnaces installed globally; the mature baseline for electric melting.

companies.name: ENRX
companies.what: Induction heating and contactless power specialist formed from EFD Induction + Radyne merger (2023).
companies.signal: Global installed base across automotive, tube/pipe and forging heat treatment.

companies.name: Kanthal
companies.what: Electric heating elements, modules and MW-class electric process-gas heaters (Alleima group) enabling furnace electrification to 1,000C+.
companies.signal: Supplies resistive heating technology into e-cracker, calciner and TES projects industry-wide.

variations.white_space: Beyond mature induction/IR niches, plasma, microwave and e-beam stay confined to high-value applications because capex per MW, electrode/magnetron lifetime, and RF coupling physics limit general-purpose heat; the wedge that is working is drop-in burner-replacement retrofits inside existing furnaces (PyroGenesis' aluminum play, Coolbrook's kiln heater) rather than whole-furnace rebuilds.

variations.name: Electrified steam crackers, calciners, and glass/metal furnaces
variations.description: Rebuilds the hottest core equipment of heavy industry - steam crackers, lime/cement calciners, and glass melting furnaces - around electric heating, eliminating the largest point-source combustion emissions in chemicals and minerals while enabling pure CO2 capture streams.

companies.name: BASF
companies.what: Operates the world's first MW-scale electrically heated steam-cracking furnace demo (with SABIC and Linde) at Ludwigshafen, cutting cracker CO2 ~90%.
companies.signal: Demo plant in operation since April 2024 testing direct and indirect heating concepts at 6 MW.

companies.name: Linde Engineering
companies.what: Built the BASF/SABIC e-cracker demo and is commercializing electrified furnace technology under the STARBRIDGE brand.
companies.signal: EPC of the world-first e-furnace demo; licensing pipeline to petrochemical operators.

companies.name: Dow-Shell e-cracker program
companies.what: Joint development of e-cracking furnace technology; experimental unit started 2022 targeting a multi-megawatt pilot.
companies.signal: No public progress updates since the 2022 experimental startup; program status unclear - evidence of how hard e-cracking economics are.

companies.name: SaltX Technology
companies.what: Stockholm-listed developer of the Electric Arc Calciner for zero-emission quicklime/cement with inherent CO2 capture.
companies.signal: ZEQL venture with SMA Mineral building world's first electric zero-emission quicklime plant at Mo i Rana, Norway (kiln by thyssenkrupp Polysius, factory target 2027); EAC lime used in steelmaking trial Q1 2025.

companies.name: Fives
companies.what: French engineering group supplying Prium E-Melt all-electric glass melting furnaces.
companies.signal: Delivered world's largest all-electric container-glass furnace (160-180 tpd, with Verallia, ~60% CO2 cut); strategic e-furnace deal with Pochet for luxury glass.

companies.name: Verallia
companies.what: Glass packaging maker operating the world's first 100% electric furnace for flint container glass at commercial scale.
companies.signal: 180 t/day all-electric furnace producing ~300,000 bottles/day in France.

companies.name: Coolbrook (RDR e-cracking)
companies.what: RotoDynamic Reactor replacing gas-fired cracking furnaces with electric shock-wave heating for olefins.
companies.signal: Large-scale pilot at Brightlands since 2022 with petrochemical partners; commercial cement-side deployment de-risks the platform.

variations.white_space: Only deep-pocketed incumbent consortia can fund e-cracker and e-furnace demos, and each design is a bespoke one-off tied to a single site; the open ground is licensable modular electric furnace/calciner packages (SaltX's licensing model) and grid-integration layers that let multi-MW furnaces flex against power prices.

variations.name: Concentrated solar industrial heat and steam
variations.description: Mirrors, enclosed troughs, Fresnel lines and vacuum flat-plate collectors concentrate sunlight into 100-400C+ steam and heat for factories, displacing fuel directly where land and sunshine are abundant - a sector with strong physics but a brutal commercial track record.

companies.name: GlassPoint
companies.what: Greenhouse-enclosed trough solar steam at oilfield/mining scale; relaunched 2021 after its 2020 bankruptcy (Miraah Oman legacy).
companies.signal: $1.5B Ma'aden Solar I in Saudi Arabia - world's largest planned industrial solar-steam project (target 65% of alumina refinery steam, ~600 kt CO2/yr) - in demonstration/pilot phase with MISA backing.

companies.name: Absolicon
companies.what: Swedish-listed maker of T160 concentrating collectors (160C) sold with turnkey robotized production lines licensed to partners worldwide.
companies.signal: Spotlight-listed; production-line license model across multiple countries; positioning for the EU's EUR 1B industrial heat auction.

companies.name: Naked Energy
companies.what: UK developer of VirtuHOT/VirtuPVT vacuum-tube hybrid solar thermal + PV collectors for commercial and industrial roofs.
companies.signal: Distribution partnerships (incl. E.ON) and C&I installs across Europe, US and Asia.

companies.name: TVP Solar
companies.what: Swiss high-vacuum flat-plate collectors producing steam to ~180C without tracking, for industrial sites and district heat.
companies.signal: Commissioned solar steam plant (2.2 barg, ~135C) at Shell & Vivo Lubricants blending plant, Casablanca, Oct 2025, cutting propane use ~30%.

companies.name: Azteq
companies.what: Belgian developer of linear Fresnel solar steam installations for chemical and tank-storage sites in low-DNI northern Europe.
companies.signal: Operating Fresnel steam plants at Belgian industrial sites (e.g., ADPO logistics); EU demonstration funding.

companies.name: newHeat
companies.what: French developer-financier of large flat-plate solar thermal farms supplying factories and district networks under heat-purchase agreements.
companies.signal: Multiple of France's largest solar industrial heat plants (food, malting, dairy) operating under long-term heat contracts.

companies.name: Sunvapor
companies.what: California developer of solar steam with storage for food processing and desalination (Horizon collector).
companies.signal: DOE-supported pilots circa 2018-2022; little public commercial activity since - viability unclear.

companies.name: Heliogen
companies.what: AI-aimed heliostat towers for high-temperature heat, steam and power, once hyped for cement and green hydrogen.
companies.signal: SPAC'd at ~$2B (2021), burned cash, delisted; acquired by residential installer Zeo Energy for ~$10M all-stock, completed Aug 2025.

variations.white_space: Serial failures - GlassPoint 1.0's 2020 bankruptcy, Heliogen's ~$10M fire-sale off a ~$2B SPAC - show that land, capex and intermittency rarely beat cheap PV feeding electric heat batteries; the surviving opening is very high-DNI geographies with expensive fuel and giant steady steam loads (Saudi alumina, MENA mining/desalination), and heat-purchase-agreement business models that remove customer capex.

variations.name: Geothermal direct-use heat for industrial and district process loads
variations.description: Taps hot water from conventional hydrothermal wells or engineered closed loops to feed district networks and low-temperature industrial processes with 24/7 carbon-free heat, avoiding the conversion losses of geothermal power.

companies.name: Eavor Technologies
companies.what: Closed-loop 'Eavor-Loop' conduction radiators in deep rock, dispatchable heat and power anywhere without fracking or aquifers.
companies.signal: First commercial project at Geretsried, Germany (district heat + power); backed by bp Ventures, Chevron Tech Ventures and EIB debt; deep multilateral test wells to 250C rock.

companies.name: Innargi
companies.what: A.P. Moller Holding-backed developer that finances, builds and operates large geothermal heat plants for district heating utilities.
companies.signal: 110 MW Aarhus plant - EU's largest new geothermal district heating - began supplying heat 2025 (target ~20% of city demand by 2030); expansion agreements in Poland.

companies.name: Vulcan Energy Resources
companies.what: Upper Rhine geothermal brine projects co-producing lithium and renewable heat for utilities and industry.
companies.signal: Resumed Landau geothermal heat supply to utility ESW (2025); EUR 250M EIB financing for Phase One Lionheart; all permits for combined geothermal-lithium plant.

companies.name: GreenFire Energy
companies.what: GreenLoop closed-loop retrofits that convert idle or marginal wells into heat and power producers.
companies.signal: DOE-supported closed-loop demonstrations (incl. Coso, California); early commercial agreements.

variations.white_space: Physics keeps this thin: most accessible hydrothermal resources sit below ~120C while industrial steam needs >150C, and heat cannot be shipped, so projects only work where industry happens to sit on the resource and drilling capex is front-loaded; the openings are closed-loop wells serving low-temperature food/drying/aquaculture loads on sedimentary basins, co-production economics (lithium + heat, a la Vulcan), and develop-finance-operate models that take drilling risk off industrial hosts (a la Innargi).

variations.name: Waste-heat recovery and upgrading: ORC, sCO2, thermoelectric and thermoacoustic conversion
variations.description: Captures exhaust and cooling-stream heat and either reuses it or converts it to electricity via organic Rankine cycle or supercritical-CO2 turbines (with thermoelectric and thermoacoustic routes still niche), cutting fuel and power demand without touching the core process.

companies.name: Echogen Power Systems
companies.what: Supercritical-CO2 heat-to-power cycles (EPS100) for industrial exhaust and gas-turbine bottoming, plus pumped-thermal storage variants.
companies.signal: DOE/ARPA-E-backed Ohio developer; licensing-led model with utility and industrial partners; sCO2 remains at demonstration scale.

companies.name: Climeon
companies.what: Swedish-listed modular HeatPower 300 ORC converting 80-120C waste heat to power for ships and industry.
companies.signal: Commissioned HeatPower 300 on a containership (2025); NEO Group PET plant unit generating ~2,700 MWh/yr; restructured 2022-23 around maritime focus.

companies.name: Orcan Energy
companies.what: Munich maker of mass-produced modular ORC 'efficiency PACKs' for engines, industry and geothermal.
companies.signal: Launched MW-class eP 1000 (Jul 2025); Howden turbomachinery collaboration (Nov 2025); large deployed fleet across marine and industrial sites.

companies.name: Turboden
companies.what: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' ORC house: utility-scale waste-heat, biomass and geothermal ORC plus large heat pumps.
companies.signal: Hundreds of ORC references; 32 MWe geothermal ORC contract for Vulcan's Lionheart lithium-heat project (2025).

companies.name: Ormat Technologies
companies.what: NYSE-listed geothermal major whose Recovered Energy Generation ORC units harvest gas-pipeline compressor and industrial waste heat.
companies.signal: Decades of REG plants operating across North America; ~GW-scale total generation fleet.

companies.name: Enogia
companies.what: French Euronext Growth-listed maker of compact micro-ORC turbines for engine and industrial waste heat.
companies.signal: Listed 2021; small-scale ORC and fuel-cell compressor lines; niche but active.

companies.name: Alphabet Energy
companies.what: Thermoelectric generator modules converting engine/industrial exhaust heat directly to power.
companies.signal: Raised ~$50M+ in VC; shut down in 2018 when thermoelectric $/W never approached parity - the cautionary tale for solid-state waste-heat conversion.

variations.white_space: Heat-exchanger reuse is mature and MW-scale ORC is crowded, but conversion below ~1 MW and all solid-state routes (thermoelectric, thermoacoustic) remain uneconomic - Alphabet Energy's shutdown closed that chapter; openings are zero-capex heat-to-power-as-a-service for mid-size factories and proving sCO2 at >10 MW where its compactness beats steam.

variations.name: Fuel-flexible decarbonized combustion: hydrogen-ready and biogas burners, oxyfuel
variations.description: Keeps combustion but decarbonizes it - burners engineered to fire hydrogen, biogas and low-grade fuels, plus oxygen-enriched (oxyfuel) firing that cuts fuel use 20-30% and concentrates CO2 for capture - the pragmatic bridge for heat beyond electrification's current reach.

companies.name: Zeeco
companies.what: Major US burner/flare/incineration maker offering process burners rated for up to 100% hydrogen firing in refinery and chemical heaters.
companies.signal: Global installed base across refining/petrochem; H2-capable burner retrofits a growth line.

companies.name: John Zink Hamworthy (Koch)
companies.what: Koch Engineered Solutions' combustion arm supplying hydrogen-ready process burners and large retrofit/aftermarket programs.
companies.signal: One of the two dominant process-burner franchises worldwide.

companies.name: ClearSign Technologies
companies.what: NASDAQ-listed (CLIR) developer of ultra-low-NOx, hydrogen-capable process burners for refinery heaters and boilers.
companies.signal: Microcap with slow multi-year commercial ramp; installs with US refiners and boiler OEM partnerships - evidence of how hard burner disruption is.

companies.name: SAACKE
companies.what: German industrial/marine combustion specialist firing hydrogen, biogas, lean gases and multi-fuel mixes.
companies.signal: Long-standing global burner installed base; H2 and low-CV fuel lines commercial.

companies.name: WS Warmeprozesstechnik
companies.what: Inventor of FLOX flameless-oxidation recuperative burners, hydrogen-capable, for high-temperature furnace efficiency and near-zero NOx.
companies.signal: FLOX technology deployed across heat-treatment and steel furnaces; H2-FLOX demonstrations.

companies.name: Linde
companies.what: Industrial-gas major supplying oxyfuel combustion systems (e.g., OPTIMELT regenerative) that cut glass/metal furnace fuel use and enable CO2 capture.
companies.signal: Commercial oxyfuel references across glass and metals worldwide.

variations.white_space: The burner market is locked up by incumbents and a burner swap is cheap insurance compared to full electrification, leaving startups little room - ClearSign's decade-long struggle as a listed microcap is the proof; the realistic openings are certified 100%-hydrogen retrofit packages, combustion sensing/AI tuning layers, and oxyfuel-plus-capture integration rather than new burner hardware.

variations.name: AI process-heat optimization and digital-twin software
variations.description: Closed-loop AI, reinforcement learning and physics-based digital twins continuously retune furnaces, boilers, steam systems and heat networks, typically shaving 5-15% of fuel and emissions with zero new process hardware - the fastest-payback decarbonization lever.

companies.name: Imubit
companies.what: Closed-loop reinforcement-learning optimization that directly writes setpoints for refinery and petrochemical units.
companies.signal: ~$50M raised; deployed at dozens of US refining/petrochemical plants in closed loop.

companies.name: Phaidra
companies.what: Ex-DeepMind team building autonomous AI control agents for industrial cooling and thermal plants, now centered on data-center 'AI factories'.
companies.signal: $50M+ Series B (Oct 2025) led by Collaborative Fund with NVIDIA and Index participation.

companies.name: Gradyent
companies.what: Real-time physics + AI digital twins optimizing district and industrial heating/cooling grids end to end.
companies.signal: EUR 28M Series B (Apr 2025, Blue Earth Capital); customers incl. Veolia, Shell and Helen; revenue tripled in under three years.

companies.name: AspenTech
companies.what: Industry-standard advanced process control and optimization suite (Aspen DMC3, GDOT) across refining and chemicals; majority-owned by Emerson.
companies.signal: Thousands of plant deployments; the incumbent layer new AI entrants must beat or integrate with.

companies.name: Honeywell
companies.what: Forge/UOP process optimization, APC and connected thermal/combustion services spanning its huge controls installed base.
companies.signal: Global DCS+APC incumbency gives default distribution for heat-optimization software.

variations.name: High-efficiency motors and drives
variations.description: Ultra-efficient motor architectures (PCB-stator axial-flux, synchronous reluctance, switched reluctance) paired with variable-frequency drives cut the electricity wasted by the pumps, fans, compressors and conveyors that consume most industrial power - freeing grid headroom and budget for electrified heat.

companies.name: Infinitum
companies.what: Axial-flux 'Aircore' motors with printed-circuit-board stators and integrated VFDs, ~50% smaller/lighter at IE5+ efficiency.
companies.signal: $220M total Series E (led by Just Climate, extended 2025 with Marunouchi); DOE clean-manufacturing award; Fast Company #1 energy innovator 2025.

companies.name: Turntide Technologies
companies.what: Switched-reluctance smart motor systems; refocused on electrification powertrains and battery systems after divesting building automation.
companies.signal: Former unicorn (> $600M raised) hit repeated layoffs 2022-24; automation division sold to BrainBox AI (May 2024); Hitachi Rail LFP battery contract (Jul 2025).

companies.name: ECM PCB Stator Tech
companies.what: Design platform and licensing for PCB-stator electric motors enabling compact high-efficiency machines for OEMs.
companies.signal: Venture-backed; OEM design wins across HVAC, marine and robotics niches.

companies.name: ABB
companies.what: Global motors/drives leader; IE5 ultra-premium synchronous-reluctance motor + VFD packages with massive service network.
companies.signal: Mature, widely deployed IE5 SynRM line; benchmark for industrial efficiency retrofits.

companies.name: WEG
companies.what: Brazilian motors giant shipping high-efficiency IE4/IE5 motors and drives at global scale and aggressive cost points.
companies.signal: One of the world's largest motor manufacturers with growing energy-efficiency portfolio.

companies.name: Danfoss
companies.what: VFD powerhouse (VLT/Vacon) plus system-level decarbonization engineering for motor-driven loads.
companies.signal: Among the largest global drives installed bases; drives attach directly to heat-pump and electrification projects.
